name: Björk
hook: An Icelandic punk singer who moved to London, called house the only truly modern pop music, and made her solo records with the producers of British club music.
blurb: Björk was born in Reykjavík, Iceland, on 21 November 1965 and made her first album there as a child, in 1977. In the 1980s she was the singer of the Sugarcubes, an Icelandic band that became known around the world. When they stopped in 1992 she moved to London and went solo. She said at the time that house music was the only really modern pop music being made, and she chose producers from British dance music. 'Debut' (July 1993) was made with Nellee Hooper, who had worked with Soul II Soul and was part of the Bristol circle around Massive Attack, and drew on London club culture. 'Post' (1995) brought in Graham Massey of 808 State, Tricky and Howie B, and 'Homogenic' (1997) was built with Mark Bell of the Warp electronic group LFO, setting strings against harsh programmed beats. Her records mix strings and electronic beats with her very unusual voice. Radiohead name 'Homogenic' as one of the influences on 'Kid A'. 'Fossora' (2022) was the first album she produced entirely alone.

signatureTracks.title: Human Behaviour
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The first single from 'Debut', with Nellee Hooper: a pop song on a club beat.

signatureTracks.title: Hyperballad

signatureTracks.title: Jóga
